title.tr: Yeni ev, ilk cümleler: είμαι ve έχω
title.en: A new flat, first sentences: είμαι and έχω

blocks.tr:
Bu bölümde **selam vermeyi**, **adını ve nereli olduğunu söylemeyi**, bir şeyin **nerede olduğunu sormayı** ve neyin **olduğunu** söylemeyi öğreneceksin.

Bunun için iki fiil yeter: **είμαι** (olmak: *-im*) ve **έχω** (sahip olmak: *-im var*). İkisi Yunancadaki en sık fiiller.
blocks.en:
In this chapter you learn to **greet people**, **say your name and where you are from**, **ask where something is**, and say what you **have**.

Two verbs are enough for all of it: **είμαι** (to be) and **έχω** (to have). They are the two commonest verbs in Greek.

blocks.tr:
Yeni bir eve taşındın. Ev sahibine ilk ne sorarsın? Mutfak nerede, banyo nerede, balkon var mı?

Türkçede ev sahibine *siz*, yaşıtın komşuna *sen* dersin. Yunancada da aynısını yapacaksın.
blocks.en:
You have just moved into a new flat. What do you ask the landlady first? Where is the kitchen, where is the bathroom, is there a balcony?

You would speak politely to the landlady and casually to a neighbour your age. Greek marks that difference in the words themselves, like French *vous* and *tu*.

blocks.tr: Önce iki diyaloğu dinle (▶ Hepsini dinle), sonra oku. Bilmediğin kelimeye dokun. Çeviriyi en sona bırak.
blocks.en: Listen to both dialogues first (▶ Play all), then read them. Tap any word you don't know. Leave the translation for last.

setting.tr: Akşam, Kalamarya'da bir apartman. Zeynep, ev sahibi Katerina Hanım'ın kapısını çalıyor.
setting.en: Evening, a block of flats in Kalamaria. Zeynep knocks on the door of her landlady, Mrs Katerina.

lines.el: Καλησπέρα σας! Είστε η κυρία Ζεϊνέπ;
lines.tr: İyi akşamlar! Zeynep Hanım siz misiniz?
lines.en: Good evening! Are you Ms Zeynep?

lines.el: Ναι, καλησπέρα. Με λένε Ζεϊνέπ Αϊντίν.
lines.tr: Evet, iyi akşamlar. Adım Zeynep Aydın.
lines.en: Yes, good evening. My name is Zeynep Aydın.

lines.el: Χαίρω πολύ. Εγώ είμαι η Κατερίνα. Από πού είστε;
lines.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Katerina. Where are you from?

lines.el: Από την Τουρκία. Είμαι από τη Σμύρνη.
Ορίστε το κλειδί. Εδώ είναι η κουζίνα.
lines.en: Here is the key. This is the kitchen.

lines.el: Εκεί. Και το σπίτι έχει δύο δωμάτια.
lines.tr: Orada. Bir de evde iki oda var.
lines.en: Over there. And the flat has two rooms.
Thank you very much, Mrs Katerina.

setting.tr: Biraz sonra, merdivende. Katerina Hanım'ın oğlu Giorgos yukarı çıkıyor.
setting.en: A little later, on the stairs. Mrs Katerina's son Giorgos is coming up.

lines.el: Γεια σου! Εσύ είσαι η Ζεϊνέπ;
Ναι! Γεια σου. Πώς σε λένε;
Με λένε Γιώργο. Είμαι ο γείτονας.
lines.en: My name is Giorgos. I'm the neighbour.

lines.el: Κι εγώ. Έχεις τραπέζι στην κουζίνα;
lines.tr: Ben de. Mutfakta masan var mı?
lines.en: Me too. Do you have a table in the kitchen?

lines.el: Όχι, δεν έχω. Έχω ένα χαλί και ένα φλιτζάνι!
lines.tr: Hayır, yok. Bir halım ve bir fincanım var!
lines.en: No, I don't. I have a rug and a cup!

lines.el: Εμείς έχουμε ένα τραπέζι. Είναι για σένα!
lines.tr: Bizim bir masamız var. Senin olsun!
lines.en: We have a table. It's yours!

blocks.tr: Üç küçük not: [[δωμάτια]], *δωμάτιο* kelimesinin çoğulu (çoğul alışveriş bölümünde gelecek). [[στην κουζίνα]] "mutfakta" demek; *σε* + artikel kuralı ulaşım bölümünde. [[για σένα]] "senin için".
blocks.en: Three small notes: [[δωμάτια]] is the plural of *δωμάτιο* (the plural comes in the shopping chapter). [[στην κουζίνα]] means "in the kitchen"; the rule for *σε* + article comes in the chapter on getting around. [[για σένα]] means "for you".
Two short questions on the dialogues.

blocks.tr: Yunancada fiilin sonu kimin konuştuğunu söyler; tıpkı Türkçede *İzmirli-yim*, *İzmirli-sin* gibi. Bu yüzden *εγώ* (ben), *εσύ* (sen) gibi zamirleri çoğu zaman söylemezsin: [[Είμαι από τη Σμύρνη.]] yeter. Zamiri yalnızca vurgu için kullanırsın: [[Εγώ είμαι η Κατερίνα.]] ("Katerina *benim*").
blocks.en: In Greek the verb's ending tells you who is speaking, so the pronouns *εγώ* (I), *εσύ* (you) and so on are usually left out: [[Είμαι από τη Σμύρνη.]] is enough. You add the pronoun only for emphasis: [[Εγώ είμαι η Κατερίνα.]] ("*I* am Katerina").

note.tr: *είστε* iki işe yarar: birden çok kişiye konuşurken ve tek bir kişiye resmî konuşurken; tam Türkçedeki *siz* gibi. Katerina Hanım Zeynep'e [[Από πού είστε;]] diye soruyor.
note.en: *είστε* does two jobs: talking to several people, and talking politely to one person. Mrs Katerina asks Zeynep [[Από πού είστε;]].

blocks.tr:
*έχω* "bende … var" demek. Türkçede *halım var* dersin; Yunancada "halıya sahibim" der gibi: [[Έχω ένα χαλί.]]

Bir yerde ne olduğunu da *έχει* ile söylersin: [[Το σπίτι έχει μπαλκόνι.]] "Evin balkonu var." Olumsuz için fiilin önüne *δεν*: [[Δεν έχω.]] "Yok."
blocks.en:
*έχω* means "I have": [[Έχω ένα χαλί.]]

To say what a place has, use *έχει*: [[Το σπίτι έχει μπαλκόνι.]] "The flat has a balcony." For "not", put *δεν* before the verb: [[Δεν έχω.]] "I don't (have one)."

note.tr: Bu altı sonu iyi öğren: Yunanca fiillerin çoğu aynen böyle çekilir. Bir sonraki bölümde onlarca fiile uygulayacaksın.
note.en: Learn these six endings well: most Greek verbs go exactly like this. In the next chapter you will use them on many verbs.

title.tr: ο, η, το: her ismin bir cinsi var
title.en: ο, η, το: every noun has a gender

blocks.tr:
Yunancada her ismin bir **cinsi** var: eril, dişil ya da nötr. Cinsi, ismin önündeki **artikel** gösterir: *ο*, *η* ya da *το* (Türkçede karşılığı yok; İngilizcedeki *the* gibi). Masanın erkek ya da kadın olmasıyla ilgisi yok; bu bir dilbilgisi etiketi.

İsmin sonu çoğu zaman ipucu verir. Ama en güvenlisi her ismi artikeliyle birlikte öğrenmek: *καφές* değil, **ο καφές**.
blocks.en:
Every Greek noun has a **gender**: masculine, feminine or neuter. The **article** in front of it shows which: *ο*, *η* or *το* (all three mean "the"). It has nothing to do with the thing itself: a table is not male or female; it is a grammatical label.

The ending is often a clue. But the safest habit is to learn every noun with its article: not *καφές*, but **ο καφές**.

blocks.tr: Bu bölümün kelimeleri. ▶ ile dinle. Bölümü bitirince oturumlarına gelecekler; her biri sana sorulmadan önce bir kez gösterilecek.
blocks.en: The words of this chapter. Listen with ▶. Once you finish the chapter they come into your sessions, and each one is shown to you once before you are asked it.

blocks.tr: **Sen ve siz.** [[Γεια σου]] samimi, [[Γεια σας]] resmî ya da birden çok kişiye; *σου* "senin", *σας* "sizin" demek. Türkçede bunu zaten yapıyorsun: Katerina Hanım'a *siz*, Giorgos'a *sen*.
blocks.en: **Formal and informal.** [[Γεια σου]] is informal, [[Γεια σας]] is formal or for several people: *σου* is "your" to one friend, *σας* "your" politely or to many. Like French *tu* and *vous*: Zeynep says *σας* to Mrs Katerina and *σου* to Giorgos.

blocks.tr: **Erkek adlarının sonundaki -ς.** *Γιώργος* "Giorgos" demek; ama ona seslenirken ve *με λένε* sözünden sonra sondaki -ς düşer: [[Με λένε Γιώργο.]] [[Χαίρω πολύ, Γιώργο!]] Kadın adları değişmez: [[Με λένε Κατερίνα.]]
blocks.en: **The -ς of men's names.** *Γιώργος* is the name; but when you call him, and after *με λένε*, the final -ς goes: [[Με λένε Γιώργο.]] [[Χαίρω πολύ, Γιώργο!]] Women's names do not change: [[Με λένε Κατερίνα.]]

blocks.tr: **πού ve που.** Vurgulu [[πού;]] "nerede?" demek. Vurgusuz *που* başka bir kelime ("ki, olan"); ona sonra geleceğiz. Soru sorarken vurguyu unutma.
blocks.en: **πού and που.** With the accent, [[πού;]] means "where?". Without it, *που* is a different word ("that, who"), which comes later. When you ask, keep the accent.

blocks.tr: Sözlü sınav hep böyle bir sohbetle başlar: [[Πώς σας λένε; Από πού είστε;]] Görevli seninle resmî konuşur. Kısa ama tam cümleyle cevap ver: **Με λένε … Είμαι από την Τουρκία.**
blocks.en: The speaking exam always opens with a chat like this: [[Πώς σας λένε; Από πού είστε;]] The examiner speaks to you formally. Answer briefly, in full sentences: **Με λένε … Είμαι από την Τουρκία.**

blocks.tr: Şimdi sen dene. Yanlış yapmak serbest: bunlar sınav hazırlığı hesabına girmez.
blocks.en: Now you try. Mistakes are fine here: these do not count towards your exam readiness.
